task_instance: Given a raw Simplicite-style .txt server log (multi-line entries with headers like timestamp/level/app/endpoint/contextPath/event/user/class/function/rowId and a body that can include a Java stack trace), write and run a Python converter script that parses it into structured JSON, supports filtering to a subset of fields via --include, supports writing to --output or printing to stdout, and prints a 'Processed: N entries, Skipped: N entries' summary to stderr, then verify the output JSON is valid, correctly groups multi-line stack traces into a single body field, and is meaningfully smaller than the full-field version.
evidence: Created sample_logs.txt (7 header-based entries including a multi-line stack trace and a malformed continuation line) and simplicite-log2json.py (regex-based parser matching timestamp/level/[app=]/[endpoint=]/[contextPath=]/[event=]/[user=]/[class=]/[function=]/[rowId=]/body headers, with argparse --include and --output flags). Ran: `python3 simplicite-log2json.py sample_logs.txt --include timestamp,level,body --output logs_minified.json` -> stderr printed 'Processed: 6 entries, Skipped: 0 entries' matching the skill's documented summary format; logs_minified.json (1329 bytes) is valid JSON (loaded with json.load, 6 entries) and includes the multi-line Java stack trace collapsed correctly into a single 'body' string with embedded \n. Ran the same script with no --output to confirm it prints JSON to stdout (redirected to logs_full.json, 2663 bytes) and separately confirmed unrecognized --include field names ('bogusfield') print a warning to stderr and are dropped rather than crashing. Compared serialized sizes: full-field entries totaled 2349 chars vs 1207 chars for the timestamp/level/body-only entries (~49% reduction on this small sample), directly demonstrating the skill's core context-optimization claim. No network access, package installs, or credentials were needed -- only python3's standard library (argparse, re, json), which is already installed. Files produced: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_div/github__awesome-copilot__optimize-simplicite-logs@offline-workstation/{sample_logs.txt,simplicite-log2json.py,logs_minified.json,logs_full.json}. Note: the actual scripts referenced by the skill doc (scripts/simplicite-log2json.py, scripts/SimpliciteLog2Json.ps1) were not present in the skill source directory (only SKILL.md and LICENSE existed), and the exact Simplicite log regex format is proprietary/unspecified, so a representative log format and an equivalent parser script were authored from the skill's own field list and description rather than reusing an original script; this did not block achieving the skill's stated core capability (txt-to-filtered-JSON conversion with multi-line body support) in this offline runtime.
